title: Neural tissue mapped — selected datasets
description: Physical volume checkpoints in selected synapse-resolution imaging and reconstruction datasets, with species and volume basis kept distinct.
coverage: Selected global evidence across human, mouse, and fruit fly datasets; not an exhaustive inventory or worldwide cumulative volume.
caveat: Sample bounds, imaged volume, and neuropil volume are not interchangeable. Reconstruction completeness varies; no cross-dataset lines, sums, or global growth rate.

tracks.label: Bock mouse cortex · imaged bounds
tracks.definition: Mouse V1 serial-EM imaged tissue extent; not a saturated connectome.

points.label: Bock mouse V1
points.note: Source: “Reconstruction encompasses 450 X 350 X 52 um volume of tissue.” Derived geometric volume: 450 × 350 × 52 / 10⁹ = 0.00819 mm³. Publication-year checkpoint; first release date not established. Dense reconstruction of every neurite is not asserted.

tracks.label: Hemibrain fly · sample bounds
tracks.definition: Adult female fly central-brain sample bounding volume; segmented, synapse annotated, extensively proofread.

points.label: Hemibrain
points.note: Source: “The hemibrain sample is roughly 250 × 250 × 250 μm.” Geometric product 0.015625 mm³, displayed approximately 0.0156; not acquired voxel-mask volume. Publication year, not exact release date.

tracks.label: H01 human cortex · imaged tissue
tracks.definition: Human temporal-cortex EM sample, automatically reconstructed with selected cells proofread.

points.label: H01 first public release
points.sourceLabel: H01 first public release — primary source
points.note: Source: “roughly one cubic millimeter of brain tissue.” Announcement dated June 1, 2021. Automated segmentation and annotated synapses; only selected cells proofread. Later 1.05-mm³ compression-corrected paper estimate is not new tissue.

tracks.label: MICrONS mouse cortex · imaged tissue
tracks.definition: Mouse visual-cortex cubic-millimeter-class EM resource; dense automated reconstruction, selective proofreading.

points.label: MICrONS v117
points.note: Source: “first public data released on the cubic millimeter dataset in July 2021.” Approximate nominal sample scale, not an exact valid segmentation mask. July precision; 2025 paper is later analysis of this specimen.

tracks.label: FlyWire fly · neuropil volume
tracks.definition: Adult female fly whole-brain neuropil volume; not whole-specimen image volume.

points.label: FlyWire whole-brain neuropil
points.note: Source: “The whole brain contains 0.0175 mm³ of neuropil volume.” Publication-year checkpoint for this reported value; the reconstruction reuses FAFB imagery and is not new tissue acquired in 2024.

tracks.label: LICONN mouse cortex · native tissue
tracks.definition: Light-microscopy reconstruction of mouse somatosensory cortex, measured before hydrogel expansion.

points.label: LICONN native tissue
points.note: Figure 1: “0.95 × 10⁶ µm³ before” expansion, equivalent to 0.00095 mm³. Native volume, not expanded hydrogel; automated dense reconstruction with synaptic molecular predictions and selected traced validation regions. Publication-year checkpoint, first final-dataset release not established.

tracks.label: MaleCNS fly · imaged volume
tracks.definition: Adult male fly brain and ventral nerve cord EM image volume; segmented and extensively proofread.

points.label: MaleCNS v0.9
points.note: Preprint: “0.082 mm3 total volume” (160 teravoxels at 8-nm isotropic resolution). Release date independently verified at https://male-cns.janelia.org/ : “2025-10-03 - MaleCNS v0.9 released”. Later v1.0 and 2026 publication reuse this specimen; not all synapses have proofread partners.

title: Implanted BCI participants — selected cohorts
description: Publicly identified human recipients in assistive implanted-BCI research, including intracortical, surface, endovascular, and brain-to-spine interfaces.
coverage: Selected global evidence: historical literature/disclosure cohort plus separate company/program checkpoints. Incomplete coverage, not a current worldwide total.
caveat: Cohorts overlap: do not add the review to company counts or suppliers to programs. Ever implanted is not active users. Lines join only Neuralink’s compatible cumulative checkpoints.

tracks.label: Identified global review cohort
tracks.definition: Authors’ discoverable 1998–December 2023 assistive-iBCI cohort; not an audited census.

points.label: Review cohort through Dec 2023
points.sourceLabel: Patrick-Krueger et al., Nature Reviews Bioengineering
points.note: Source: “These groups have implanted a total of 67 participants”; data collection ended December 2023 and later implants are excluded. Includes ECoG and endovascular systems, not only intracortical. Only 31 were active at cutoff. Supplement Table 2 identifies participants but does not supply implantation-year columns; no annual points invented.

tracks.label: Neuralink · cumulative recipients
tracks.definition: One company’s disclosed cumulative implanted trial participants; observation months early, disclosure dates later.

points.label: Neuralink first participant
points.note: April 12, 2024 disclosure: “In January, we conducted the first human implantation.” January is the implantation month, not an exact surgery day.

points.label: Neuralink second participant
points.note: August 21, 2024 disclosure: “Last month, Alex ... the second participant ... received his Neuralink implant.” July implantation month; cumulative two recipients.

points.label: Neuralink three participants
points.note: Source: “Today, there are three people with Telepathy: Noland, Alex, and Brad.” Disclosure date, not all three surgery dates.

points.label: Neuralink five participants
points.note: Source: “Five individuals with severe paralysis are now using Neuralink to control digital and physical devices with their thoughts.” Post-implant use supports receipt, not mere enrollment.

points.label: Neuralink 21 participants
points.note: Company headline says “21 Neuralnauts enrolled”; implantation interpretation also requires body: “higher signal quality across 18 of the subsequent 20 participants” after the first recipient. Company-reported cumulative checkpoint, not independently audited current active users. Page release date Jan 28; last modification Feb 2 is not the checkpoint.

tracks.label: Synchron · US and Australia
tracks.definition: Company-reported Stentrode recipients across SWITCH and COMMAND; overlaps historical review.

points.label: Synchron ten recipients
points.note: Issuer: “Stentrode BCIs have been placed in 10 patients with paralysis to date, across clinical trials in the U.S. and Australia.” Includes four Australian and six US recipients; do not add those subsets or add this to review baseline.

tracks.label: ONWARD ARC-BCI · brain–spine
tracks.definition: Participants receiving cortical recording implant paired with spinal stimulation; count people, not hardware.

points.label: ONWARD seven participants
points.note: Source: “Seven study participants have now received ARC-BCI Therapy.” Two additional people bring total to seven. Some historical CEA/WIMAGINE participants overlap the review; exact crosswalk unresolved.

tracks.label: Paradromics · long-term study
tracks.definition: At least one long-term Connexus Connect-One recipient; excludes temporary 2025 epilepsy recording.

points.label: Paradromics first long-term participant
points.note: June 17, 2026 issuer release: “The first participant ... was enrolled and implanted ... and will be followed and evaluated over the next six years.” Exact disclosure date, not surgery date. At least one long-term participant; earlier temporary 2025 epilepsy implantation is excluded.

title: Neural recording hours — selected datasets
description: Reported recording duration in named datasets and releases, separated by modality and access; a model-training corpus is explicitly distinct.
coverage: Selected globally scoped evidence from US and Japanese human datasets and a multi-source nonhuman-primate corpus; not a harmonized worldwide archive total.
caveat: No sums across datasets, releases, modalities, or model reuse. TUSZ includes held-out evaluation data; POYO is reused training-corpus scale. These are reported hours, not independently recomputed QC-valid subject-hours.

tracks.label: TUSZ · human scalp EEG, controlled access
tracks.definition: Maintainer-reported full seizure-corpus release sizes, including held-out evaluation; a subset of TUEG.

points.label: TUSZ v1.0.0
points.sourceLabel: Rahman et al., TUSZ release history, Table 1
points.note: Table 1 reports v1.0.0, 2017-04-17, Total Duration (Hours): 170. Full corpus size, not seizure-event duration or channel-hours. Registration-controlled data; evaluation partition withheld in accompanying poster. Versions overlap and must not be summed; unchanged totals can accompany annotation revisions.

tracks.label: AJILE12 · human intracranial, open
tracks.definition: Frozen DANDI 000055/0.220127.0436; 12 participants; open CC-BY-4.0 ECoG/depth recordings.

points.label: AJILE12 frozen release
points.note: Release metadata: “Neural recordings are available at 500 Hz from at least 64 electrodes per participant, for a total of 1280 hours.” datePublished January 27, 2022. Reported duration, not electrode-multiplied time; gaps/preprocessing mean nominal and QC-valid hours differ.

tracks.label: POYO-1 · primate spikes, training corpus
tracks.definition: Reported model-training corpus spanning seven nonhuman primates and constituent datasets with varying access; not a new unique-data release.

points.label: POYO-1 training corpus
points.note: Abstract: “over 100 hours of recordings” from seven nonhuman primates and over 158 sessions. Strict lower-bound marker, not exactly 100. Existing datasets reused for training; no new-data or wholly open-corpus claim.

tracks.label: JapanEEG · human scalp EEG, open release claim
tracks.definition: Japanese speech dataset, three participants; simultaneous EEG/EMG/audio counted once for EEG duration; author-reported CC0 OpenNeuro release.

points.label: JapanEEG descriptor
points.note: Abstract: “1020 hours of simultaneously recorded scalp electroencephalography (EEG), facial electromyography (EMG), and speech audio”; authors say released through OpenNeuro under CC0. Descriptor submission date, not verified archive upload date. Count once, not three modalities; full manifest not enumerated.
